item.title: Back on top: Christian Brothers Academy football blasts Saratoga Springs in the Class AA Super Bowl
item.description: CBA head coach Bobby Burns gets water dumped on him after his team beat Saratoga for the Section 2, Class AA title on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, at Colonie High School in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) COLONIE - The Redemption Tour reached its Section 2 conclusion Saturday. And what a crescendo it turned out to be for the Christian Brothers Academy football team. One year after getting stunned by one point in the Class AA Super Bowl against Saratoga Springs, the Brothers returned to the same Colonie High School field vs. the same opponent and authored a thorough thrashing in the title-game rematch. CBA scored six touchdowns on six possessions in the first half on its way to throttling the Blue Streaks 61-14. Last year, Saratoga Springs stunned CBA 14-13 for the championship. "Coming into the game, I was so hyped. Scoring that first touchdown just meant so much to me," said CBA senior running back Tommy Toher, who was knocked out of the 2025 title game with an injury in the first quarter, but opened Saturday's scoring on a 25-yard TD run. "The culture, the continuity and the love for each other has been there since last year. They were motivated and focused all offseason," CBA coach Bobby Burns said. "These kids are special. They really are. Yes, we have a lot of talent on this team, but they let us coach them, they trust us, they execute and play their tails off when they need to. Most of all, they have been dedicated to improving since last year. I am proud of them." Saturday's win was especially sweet for veteran CBA players who felt the sting of falling to Saratoga Springs in a driving rainstorm in the 2025 Super Bowl. But it also meant a great deal to players that either had minimal roles last year or - as in the case of senior quarterback Matt Kowalski - players who barely hit the field. Kowalski rushed for three touchdowns and passed for two on Saturday, while another one of CBA's standouts was Myles Johnson - a starter at linebacker for two years - who ran for a pair of touchdowns. "It just shows you how good this team is. People like Matt and Myles were the hardest workers of all," said CBA senior standout JT Vogel, a four-year starter at safety. "They showed up ready to work at every workout. I love those guys so much, so I am glad to see them shine." "Guys like Myles and Matt are products of the offseason work. They gained confidence and prepared themselves to do what they have done this year," Burns said. Toward the end of the opening quarter, the Blue Streaks trailed 21-0. Things never got better, as the Brothers outgained Saratoga Springs 462-6. The Blue Streaks' two touchdowns came on a kickoff return from Gavin LaFrance and a 2-yard reception by Jaden Lockrow after the Blue Streaks were set up with a short field. item.title: Watch: Arch Manning connects with Raleek Brown for clutch TD, road upset of LSU
item.description: Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) celebrates a touchdown during the game against LSU at Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Arch Manning delivered his most clutch moment yet Saturday night. The Texas football quarterback struggled mightily in the first three quarters at LSU, throwing three interceptions as the Longhorns trailed 21-13 entering the final frame. Manning then rose to the occasion on the game's final drive. And Texas, No. 6 in the College Football Playoff rankings, virtually sealed its spot in the postseason tournament and dashed the hopes of Lane Kiffin and LSU. Here's a look at his game-winning touchdown pass with just 2 seconds left, and the plays that preceded it: How Arch Manning delivered in fourth quarter. Texas needed a touchdown on its final drive in its 22-21 road win. It began the drive on Texas' 42-yard line, and Manning and the Longhorns' then faced a 3rd-and-3 with 1:28 to play. Manning generated a first down on a slant to wide receiver Ryan Wingo. He then added another first-down pass to Wingo, and he added two additional first downs with his legs. The Longhorns' march deep into LSU territory concluded with a second-and-goal at the LSU four-yard line with two seconds remaining. Manning took a shotgun snap, dropped back, then lofted a pass to running back Raleek Brown down the right sideline. Brown hauled in the pass. Texas took the lead, then escaped Baton Rougue with a clutch comeback victory on the subsequent kickoff. Arch Manning and Raleek Brown with the biggest play of their careers. Texas takes the lead with two seconds left in Baton Rouge. #HookEm https://t.co/u3JE5LjhVS - Danny Davis (@_dannydavis) November 15, 2026 ARCH MANNING COMES IN CLUTCH FOR TEXAS IN DEATH VALLEY 😱 Texas racks up its fifth top 25 win of the year! https://t.co/GKCSMckphy - ESPN (@espn) November 15, 2026 Where Texas stands after Arch Manning's clutch TD The Longhorns advanced to 8-2, 4–2 SEC with Saturday's victory. They now expect to safely qualify for the College Football Playoff as a major favorite in each of its next two games, home against Arkansas next week and at Texas A&M on Friday, Nov. 27. Texas can qualify for the SEC championship on Saturday, Dec. 5, but it would need one loss by Alabama across its last two games. Texas' championship chase could have died Saturday in Baton Rouge. Five years after winning his first interim title and four years after his first shot at undisputed gold, “Bon Gamin” finally holds the belt he’d been chasing. And while the journey included some unexpected detours, the destination always seemed inevitable. Indeed, Gane has long been one of the division’s most gifted athletes and technically-polished strikers, making it somewhat remarkable that the 36-year-old had yet to officially call himself champion. Standing across from him this evening is one of UFC’s fastest-rising Heavyweights . Just three years and one month removed from his promotional debut, Hokit — a former NFL football player — has already climbed all the way to a title opportunity. The undefeated wrestler bulldozed his way through the division ( like this ), but Gane is an entirely different challenge . item.title: Texas outlasts LSU thanks to last second heroics by Arch Manning
item.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Texas outlasts LSU thanks to last second heroics by Arch Manning appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Texas football quarterback Arch Manning received fierce criticism for his turnover marred outing versus LSU . But he pulled off the epic last second heroics with Raleek Brown at Baton Rouge Saturday. The running back Brown caught LSU off guard with his motion to the left. Manning lasered his short throw from inside LSU’s five-yard line for the final touchdown with two seconds left. Texas ultimately held on for the 22-21 victory thanks to a final special teams stop. But again, Manning overcame a multiple interception evening to pull off this epic goal line touchdown. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Arch Manning with an unreal throw with the game on the line. pic.twitter.com/5IWK8Ye55Q — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 15, 2026 Manning lifted Texas to an 8-2 overall mark while ending LSU’s pursuit of an SEC title, plus College Football Playoff berth, in season one of Lane Kiffin. But the Longhorns kept their own hopes alive for both. Texas now joins Alabama and Tennessee as the conference’s remaining eight-win teams with two regular season games left. The Longhorns own the tiebreaker with the latter SEC rival after beating them earlier this season. So the path to both Atlanta come Dec. 5 and the CFP is becoming crystallized for Texas. Manning still needed to shed the memories of his earlier picks. LSU grabbed three Manning passes, with Ty Benefield snatching two of those errant throws and took one back for the touchdown. DJ Pickett grabbed the other pick. Manning even noticeable kept moving his right arm clockwise after appearing to injure himself on a previous play. But he orchestrated one epic long scoring drive. And in the process, elevated the Longhorns’ championship vision in overcoming Death Valley in Louisiana. item.title: Islanders, Holmstrom tear through Ducks defense, 6-2
item.description: Anaheim, CA - New York Islanders right wing Simon Holmstrom (92) and center Kyle Palmieri (21) celebrate after a second period goal during a regular season NHL game between the New York Islanders and the Anaheim Ducks at Honda Center on November 14, 2026, in Anaheim, CA. ANAHEIM, Calif. – That lightning hot offensive streak of a week ago papered over plenty of the Anaheim Ducks’ defensive cracks, which have suddenly morphed into canyons as the goals have dried up. The New York Islanders scored four in the second period through a porous Ducks defense, and Simon Holmström finished off a hat trick past Lukáš Dostál, as Anaheim was cratered, 6-2, on Saturday at Honda Center. Anaheim (10-9-1, 21 points) has scored just four goals in back-to-back losses after scoring 26 goals in a five-game winning streak and five or more goals in eight straight games. Nikita Nesterenko chased down a loose puck in front for the Ducks’ opening goal in the second period, 2-1, and Cutter Gauthier continued his historic goal-scoring streak later in the middle frame. Gauthier carved out space alone in front, and Tristan Luneau sent in the hard feed for the deflection, 5-2. Gauthier tied 1998-99 Teemu Selanne for the second-longest goal-scoring streak in franchise history. Selanne also owns the longest streak in team history at 11 games (1997-98). Ben Hutton was the beneficiary of a double deflection off Ducks sticks just under two minutes into the game, but the Islanders were off to the race in the second period, as wheels came off for Anaheim’s defense. Bo Horvat netted a one-timer six seconds into the first power play of the game, 2-0. Simon Holmstrom scored his first of two 25 seconds after the Ducks’ first goal from Nesterenko, as he finished a two-on-one with Matthew Schaefer. Holmstrom scored a second five minutes later, as Dostál was slid into by Leo Carlsson, and Mitchell Chaffee put in the Islanders’ fifth, as Schaefer flew the zone for another two-on-one. Holmstrom finished off the hat trick with a one-on-one beat of Dostál’s glove in the third period, 6-2. Lukáš Dostál stopped 19 of 25 shots in his first start in over a week, when he was pulled after the first period in Calgary last Friday. Ville Husso was the back-up, as Laurent Brossoit was reassigned back to AHL San Diego yesterday. Brossoit–who won his first four starts of the five he made with the Ducks during their red hot offensive streak–was the only goalie waiver exempt, and thus he was not at risk for a claim by another team when being sent to the minors. Semyon Varlamov made 26 saves for the Islanders. Anaheim concludes its four-game homestand with the second half of a back-to-back against the Calgary Flames on Sunday before hitting the road for a four-game trip, which begins in St. Louis on Tuesday.

item.title: Steve Sarkisian dials up game-winning TD pass to Raleek Brown
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 14: Running back Raleek Brown #0 of the Texas Longhorns celebrates his touchdown during the game between Louisiana State Tigers and Texas Longhorns at Tiger Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Aric Becker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images In high-profile calls on the goal line over the last several seasons, Steve Sarkisian has come up short in tenure-defining moments. On Saturday in Baton Rouge, facing off against longtime friend and former colleague Lane Kiffin, Sarkisian faced a season-defining moment hoping to make a better call than he has in the past with six seconds remaining and Texas trailing 21-16 at the LSU 4-yard line. With no timeouts remaining, the Longhorns had no more than two plays remaining. After LSU took away some of the play calls that Sarkisian went back to over the previous two games, a condensed formation created leverage to the field with return motion from running back Raleek Brown creating a clear pre-snap picture for Arch Manning. Trying to match up with Brown in coverage, LSU linebacker Davohn Keys was slow to respond to the return motion, had to take a wide angle around the field corner, and got torched, allowing Manning to hit a one-step drop and drop an easy pass into Brown’s chest for the go-ahead, four-yard touchdown with four seconds remaining. GIVE SARKISIAN HIS CREDIT RALEEK BROWN 1 ON 1 SCORES THE LIKELY GAME-WINNING TD pic.twitter.com/tpBW0Monsp — Nash (@NashTalksTexas) November 15, 2026 The Tigers were able to take away Brown in the passing game before the final offensive play for the Horns — Brown only had three catches for four yards on his first four targets, but pitting his speed to the pylon against a slower linebacker who had to navigate traffic ultimately represented one of Sarkisian’s best goal-line play calls in his nearly six years leading the Longhorns. Manning ran to embrace the head coach who trusted him in his lowest moment as an athlete, but it wasn’t a moment to celebrate for the Texas head coach. Up 22-21, Sarkisian had to call a kneel down instead of attempting a point after the Tigers could return for a go-ahead score, and the Longhorns secured the victory on the ensuing kickoff. Reflecting on the play, Brown knew it was won before the snap when a defender didn’t follow him in motion . “I was just real happy,” Brown said . ”Whatever it takes to win.” For Texas, that’s required effective play calls from Sarkisian on the goal line in defining moments. On Saturday, he got it right with one of the single best decisions in his Longhorns tenure.

item.title: MSU football grades for the Spartans' performance against Washington
item.description: Lansing State Journal columnist Graham Couch grades Michigan State's football team after its 21-14 loss to Washington on a scale of 1-10. OFFENSE: 3 This grade should probably be an incomplete. Because MSU’s offense was doing well enough before quarterback Alessio Milivojevic went down in the second quarter with an injury. He was 7-for-12 passing for 108 yards and led a touchdown drive to open the game, which including a 30-yard pass to Bryson Williams and a 26-yard completion to Carson Gulker. Without Milivojevic, MSU had some moments offensively with backup Cam Fancher — including a fourth-down touchdown pass to Williams — but also had some moments Fancher and the Spartans would like to have back, including when he threw an interception as he tried to throw away a pass, also injuring himself on the play as he tried to twist out of a tackle. MSU ran the ball somewhat effectively, with Brandon Tullis carrying 21 times again for 82 yards. And, overall, out-gained Washington 342 yards to 332. There were times when this was an effective offense, especially with Milivojevic under center. But the penalties, inconsistencies and turnovers left the Spartans sitting at 14 points, which wasn’t enough. DEFENSE: 7 Once MSU’s defense got a handle on Washington, that was it for the Huskies for a long time. Early on, the Spartans looked like they might get gashed all night by quarterback Demond Williams Jr. and receiver Chris Lawson. But after the Huskies’ second touchdown, MSU’s defense pressured Williams and largely contained everything Washington tried to do, holding the Huskies to 41 total yards on their first four second-half drives. The Spartans only recorded one sack — Williams is elusive and good as stepping up and through pressure to gain a couple yards — but if you watched the game, you saw the work that was being done to corral him. Washington also was only able to rush for 44 yards on 22 carries. In the end, MSU’s defense needed at least one more stop and gave up a few plays on the final drive that beat them. But this was a strong effort — and could have been a winning effort. This grade would be even better if not for those two early drives and for Kenny Soares Jr.'s roughing the passer penalty, which let Washington’s first drive continue, ending in a touchdown. This might have been a different game without that drive. SPECIAL TEAMS: 5 Liam Boyd missed his only field goal attempt, wide right from 50 yards out, and that might have been costly. item.title: ‘Karma’ – Fans react to Lane Kiffin seemingly crying after LSU’s season-ruining loss to Texas
item.description: Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin’s emotional moment on the field after their 22-21 loss to the Texas Longhorns ended any hopes of making it to the College Football Playoffs. The Tigers have a 6-4 season record, going 3-4 against the SEC, after the loss to the Longhorns. Kiffin’s first full season in charge of the Tigers after his acrimonious exit from Ole Miss last season has not been a pleasant ride. The emotions of failing to lead a program like LSU to the playoffs in his first full season while continuing the team’s pattern of struggling against top-10 teams left Kiffin overwhelmed after the loss. Lane Kiffin’s tears do not earn him any sympathy from CFB fans With how Kiffin left Ole Miss and his generally boisterous nature in front of the media, fans were clearly rejoicing the apparent tears from the 51-year-old coach in his first season in charge. “The karma finding Lane Kiffin this season is something to behold,” said one seemingly happy fan . “I would cry too if I had to coach Levitt,” were the thoughts of another fan . “Arch Manning had Lane Kiffin crying on the sideline,” joked a fan . “It’s not even the slightest bit difficult (to feel bad for Kiffin) after all of the stunts he’s pulled and people he’s screwed over through the years,” said one fan, rejecting anyone having sympathy for Kiffin . “I like watching him lose… Constant Karma,” said another fan . The tears were justified as this loss was the death sentence for LSU with regard to this season, as even an undefeated season from this point on might not be enough to earn them a spot in the college football playoffs. Kiffin coached Ole Miss to the playoff last season but did not get to see the season through after being asked to leave the program for agreeing midseason to join LSU in 2026, a decision that has kept him more unpopular than ever among casual fans. This is a win for fans with no loyalties, as LSU fans and Kiffin fans will have to wait another year and pray for an improvement. item.description: Japan v Brazil - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport Legendary former Brazil striker Romario has demanded the immediate dismissal of national team head coach Carlo Ancelotti following Saturday's 3-2 friendly defeat against Japan in Singapore. Taking to social media after the loss, the 1994 World Cup winner urged the Italian tactician to leave his post and return to club management. Iconic striker loses patience completely Romario has called on Brazilian Football Confederation president Samir Xaud to sack Ancelotti before the five-time world champions slide into a deeper crisis. Despite suffering a last-16 elimination against Norway at the 2026 World Cup, the Italian had his contract extended until 2030 . item.title: Hopewell’s TreVeyon Henderson placed on injured reserve by Patriots
item.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson was placed on injured reserve Nov. 14 by the team as the former Hopewell High School star battles unexplained neurological symptoms that hospitalized him. The move means that Henderson, who has not played in a game since Oct. 22, is guaranteed to miss the next four weeks. He will be re-evaluated later to determine whether he will be done for the season. The Patriots, who are in Munich, Germany this weekend for a game against the Detroit Lions, listed the reason as “illness” for Henderson’s placement on IR. No timetable was given for his return. If cleared to play, the earliest Henderson could return to the field would be Dec. 21 for a home game against the Buffalo Bills . Henderson announced his condition in a post on his X account, saying he had been hospitalized after suffering an unknown neurological episode. Neither he nor the team has confirmed if Henderson remains in the hospital as his X post asked for privacy. Henderson starred at Hopewell High School where he led the Blue Devils to the 2019 state championship. A highly sought-after recruit, he signed with Ohio State and was part of the Buckeyes’ 2024 national championship team. He was drafted in the second round by the Patriots in 2025. In Henderson’s rookie season, he rushed for 911 yards and nine touchdowns, and the Patriots reached Super Bowl XL. Before illness sidelined him, Henderson had rushed 52 times for 203 yards and one touchdown this season. Getty Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman closed his postgame interview Saturday by paying tribute to recently deceased NBC broadcaster Dan Hicks, and sending condolences to Hicks’ family. Hicks, the network’s play-by-play voice for Fighting Irish football, was scheduled to call the 41-7 Fighting Irish win over Boston College — until his sudden death three days earlier, a loss that remains largely unexplained. Freeman was discussing his team’s preparation when he turned to Hicks, who died Wednesday at age 64. “The preparation is what matters. And I want to make sure before we leave, I send our condolences out to the family of Dan Hicks and Hannah,” Freeman said, in a video posted by NBC Sports. “Just know that we’re thinking about the family, and we’re praying for them all.” He was referring also to Hannah Storm, longtime ESPN anchor and Hicks’ wife of more than 30 years. She also holds a Notre Dame degree, class of 1983. Notre Dame Fighting Irish Coach Marcus Freeman’s Dan Hicks Tribute Getty Head coach Marcus Freeman of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish. Saturday marked the second time in three days that Freeman spoke publicly about Hicks. The coach put the subject first at his Thursday media session. “I wanted to make sure we start off by sending my condolences to Hannah Storm and her daughters, and all those affected by the loss of Dan Hicks,” Freeman said, as quoted by Awful Announcing . “Dan was amazing to work with, and he was an ultimate professional, but more importantly, he was a great husband, father, and man.” Hicks first called Notre Dame games from 2013 through 2016, then came back to the booth in 2024, Freeman’s third year in charge, according to a Sports Illustrated report . That adds up to seven seasons. His final Irish telecast was the Oct. 10 victory over Stanford. Athletic director Pete Bevacqua, a former NBC Sports executive, called Hicks “a fixture here on campus and in the broadcast booth as one of the great voices for Notre Dame Football,” in a statement quoted by the South Bend Tribune . Jason Benetti took over play-by-play duties Saturday, according to The Hollywood Reporter . He worked alongside analyst Jason Garrett on a broadcast that included tributes to Hicks, according to USA Today . Notre Dame improved to 9-1 with its 11th consecutive win over Boston College . The Irish defense held the Eagles to 136 yards of total offense. Quarterback CJ Carr completed 20 of 26 passes for 217 yards and two touchdowns, while freshman running back Jonaz Walton piled up 141 rushing yards and a touchdown . Mowbray was impressed by Swansea's high-pressing approach, and said facing Vitor Matos' team brought back memories of tackling Klopp's Reds side. "Liverpool of those days were absolutely amazing because they didn't let you breathe, and you can see bits of that with this team," Mowbray said. The numbers show there is substance behind the praise. Under Matos, Swansea have developed into one of the Championship's most aggressive pressing sides, leading the division across a number of key metrics and regularly winning possession high up the pitch. That approach helped Swansea collect 23 points from their opening 10 league games, although they have since lost momentum. The Swans have won just one of their past five matches, with defeats against West Ham, Queens Park Rangers, Portsmouth and Birmingham City. Despite the downturn in results, Swansea's pressing numbers remain among the division's best. Their issues come, it appears, when they have possession, rather than when they are hunting it down. While Matos' side continue to force mistakes and create opportunities from turnovers, they sit just 12th for goals scored and 19th for total shots, highlighting a disconnect between one of the league's most effective presses and the team's attacking output. Having spent six years at Liverpool as part of Klopp's coaching staff, the Portuguese coach has spoken about the influence the German has had on his football philosophy. item.title: What is FTP? Explaining ICC's Future Tours Program
item.description: What is FTP? Explaining ICC's Future Tours Program originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Cricket’s master calendar is being reworked in Bali as the current cycle nears conclusion. Debates over ODIs, WTC expansion and franchise windows could reshape the matches fans watch. The programme has been overhauled several times since 2006, reshaping how bilateral cricket works. ICC Future Tours Programme explained: How cricket's master schedule balances bilateral series, World Cups, and T20 leagues Every cricket fan has come across the term FTP at some point, yet few could explain exactly how the Future Tours Programme decides which teams meet, where they play and why certain series return again and again while others quietly disappear from the schedule. The subject is back in the headlines because the ICC held its final Board and Committee meetings of 2026 in Bali from November 11 to 15. It was the first time the governing body has met in Indonesia. The present cycle ends in March 2027, and the final plan for 2027 to 2031 was expected to be presented at this November gathering. The Future Tours Programme is the official multi-year master calendar issued by the International Cricket Council. It maps out every bilateral international tour in Tests, ODIs and T20Is, and it places the ICC’s own global tournaments alongside them across a fixed cycle that usually runs between four and five years. Its main purpose is to bring certainty, fairness and commercial stability to the boards that play international cricket. Teams know well in advance whom they will host and whom they will visit, which allows broadcasters, sponsors, venues and players to plan their years. The calendar also reserves protected windows for ICC events such as World Cups, the Champions Trophy and the World Test Championship final, as well as for major domestic T20 leagues like the IPL. MORE: Former Aussie star reconfirms everyone knew about Sandpapergate How the FTP works: What it covers and how bilateral series get agreed The ICC sets the broad framework, but the individual series are not handed down from above. Member boards negotiate them directly with each other, and the agreed tours are then signed off through formal Members’ Participation Agreements. This means a board cannot simply walk away from a scheduled series without facing financial or legal consequences. There isn’t a single programme for everyone. Separate calendars exist for different groups of teams: The men’s FTP covers the 12 Full Members: India, Australia, England, South Africa, New Zealand, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the West Indies, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe, Ireland and Afghanistan. The Women’s FTP covers 11 nations in the 2025–2029 cycle and runs alongside the ICC Women’s Championship. item.title: Alexandra Ignatova has a new name, new title (mom) and new approach to figure skating
item.description: EVERETT, Wash. -- So much is different for Alexandra Trusova. Even her surname, which is that of her husband of two years, Makar Ignatov, in its female version, Ignatova. The Russian teenager who eight years ago led the quadruple jump revolution in women’s figure skating — and reacted with childlike petulance when her record-setting five free skate quads were not good enough to win the singles gold medal at the 2022 Olympics — is now a 22-year-old woman and mother of a 15-month-old son, Mikhail. Between 2022 and now, her country has become a pariah because of its unprovoked invasion of Ukraine. She was able to start competing internationally again this season only under a special status as an “Individual Neutral Athlete.” SKATE AMERICA: Full Results | Broadcast Schedule Motherhood gives her another special status, since she is believed to be the first mother to compete in singles skating since Japan’s Miki Ando did it briefly in the 2013-14 season. She no longer is the jumping marvel known as the “Quad Queen.” As a skater, she is more of a person in full, one who can interpret a program rather than simply run from jump to jump. Ignatova showed that in Saturday afternoon’s short program at Saatva Skate America. A gossamer dress accentuated her flowing movement to music from the film “Lara,” as choregraphed by Frenchman Benoit Richaud. “I did skate to more slow, more lyrical music before (in) one year. But now I know better how to skate to this kind of music,” she said through a translator after taking second in the short to a dazzling performance by Japan’s Ami Nakai, the 2026 Olympic bronze medalist. Ignatova is plainly delighted to be back in the arena, an attitude that sharply contrasted to her previous workmanlike demeanor on the ice. “Yes, I do enjoy really,” she said. “Otherwise, why would I do it? “When you are young, and you don't know another life, you just do what you have been doing since you were 4 years old. You go towards your goal. Because of this, you're forgetting that you need to love what you're doing. “Therefore, when I came back, I knew that I want to do this, and I love to do this, and that's why I'm enjoying it.” She has made her life something of an open book in frequent Instagram posts. She recently recounted her long trip to Everett with Mikhail from last week’s Cup of China event, in which she took second, and a shopping trip here that left her wondering how she would get all her purchases back to Russia. Either her mother or husband travels with her and her son. Her mother went to China and returned home. Ignatov met her in Washington. She was disappointed to find out there would be no exhibition gala at Skate America, so there would be no chance for her to do side-by-side quadruple Lutz jumps with Ilia Malinin. He had a Lutz among three clean quads (in four attempts) while finishing second to Italy’s Daniel Grassl Saturday night’s free skate. Malinin wound up first overall. item.title: ‘He Needs Therapy,’ ‘Hope He’s Surrounded by the Right People’ — NFL Fans Stand With C.J. Gardner-Johnson Over Emotional Message on Bills Move
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Buffalo Bills released veteran defensive back C.J. Gardner-Johnson on Nov. 3, ending his hopes of winning a Super Bowl with them this season. Since entering the league in 2019, Gardner-Johnson has played for or signed with seven teams, counting offseason and practice squad stints. This time, though, being cut by a contender clearly stung. He opened up about it on Instagram, and fans across the NFL have since rallied behind him. NFL Fans Have C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s Back In his post, Gardner-Johnson wrote about feeling abandoned in the wake of his release and said he has spent years dealing with pain on his own. “In just a couple of weeks, everyone turned on me,” he wrote . “No friends, no real support. It sucks that we live in a society where one move can cause a downfall for anything! “If this is the last time y’all see my face or hear from me, it’s cause you don’t understand the person who went through years of pain, alone, suffering, trying to fit in, and never got the same opportunity everybody else got!” Several fans took to social media to show their support. One Eagles fan wrote about how Gardner-Johnson has always played with his heart on his sleeve. “Eagles fans know C.J. Gardner-Johnson has always worn his emotions on his sleeve. Love him or hate him, nobody should feel the way he’s describing in this post. Hope he’s surrounded by the right people,” they wrote. Another fan had a more straightforward message . “He needs therapy,” they remarked. Gardner-Johnson’s release came on the heels of an incident with Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. The veteran defensive back spat on Bowers in Week 6, drawing intense backlash. He was ejected and later suspended for one game without pay, a penalty upheld by joint hearing officer Jordy Nelson. Football is bigger than just a game. These are real people with real feelings. We got your back, C.J. Keep your head up, brother,” one Bills fan wrote . He spent three seasons there before joining the Philadelphia Eagles in 2022, and he has bounced from team to team since. Besides two stints with the Eagles and his time with the Bills, he has also played for the Detroit Lions, Houston Texans and Chicago Bears. In six games with Buffalo, Gardner-Johnson collected 26 tackles and an interception, which helped him rank No. 50 in the league with a PFN Safety Impact Score of 73.1. item.title: LSU’s Lane Kiffin fell to his knees after QB Sam Leavitt threw endzone INT in close loss to Texas
item.description: Photo by Austin McAfee/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin had a fairly dramatic reaction to QB Sam Leavitt throwing his third interception of the night. Kiffin and the Tigers knew they basically needed to go undefeated for the rest of the regular season to have a chance at earning a spot in the College Football Playoffs, but they were also up against a dangerous Texas team in the same boat. Texas picked up a 22-21 win with a game-winning TD with less than five seconds left on the clock, putting a moment from Kiffin in perspective when the Tigers missed out on a chance to put the game away. Lane Kiffin’s reaction to Sam Leavitt INT tells the entire story In the third quarter of the clash, Leavitt had the opportunity to help the Tigers convert a touchdown with a pass to WR Jackson Harris in the endzone, but the pass was stolen by Texas WR/CB Jermaine Bishop Jr., prompting Kiffin to close his eyes and fall to his knees. The Tigers missed an opportunity to extend their in-game lead to over 10 points in an electric first quarter. Leavitt ended the game 27/37 on pass attempts for 244 yards and two touchdowns, but this was his third thrown interception of the clash. Leavitt did outplay Texas QB Arch Manning in many respects, but Manning successfully threw the game-winning TD when it mattered most and ended with 19/36 on pass attempts for 174 yards and one TD, along with three INTs. This was the first ranked SEC matchup since 2000 where both QBs threw three INTs, highlighting that neither QB had an especially successful evening.
